scope: Pinned-source trace plus existing E5 runtime logs; no additional model/network calls, service changes, patches, or long timeout waits.

final_sse_error.cause: An unexpected error occurred while processing the request.

iteration_exhaustion.interpretation: One endpoint call ran two OGX Responses backend invocations, each with four downstream model/tool rounds. PAI validation feedback appears at downstream request 5; final failure is output-retry exhaustion. Configured 4/6 did not act as aggregate model/tool caps.

per_backend_tool_limit.last_tool_message: Tool call skipped: maximum tool calls limit (2) reached.
per_backend_tool_limit.interpretation: A and B executed; calculate_total was skipped. The model fixture returned a partial summary, allowing this single backend response to terminate. This verifies per-response enforcement only.

ignored_configured_mcp_timeout.interpretation: Both requested 1.2-second reads finished successfully despite timeout=1. No 30/300-second transport boundary was measured.

source_findings.finding: LSCore forwards configured limits to each OGX response. A new response resets OGX inference/tool counters, and PAI can request another response for skills, function calls, or invalid/missing output.

Adding only PAI UsageLimits would count calls to the OGX Responses model abstraction and PAI function tools. Native MCP operations and downstream model rounds execute inside OGX; a top-level cap alone cannot provide the requested true aggregate counts. Current tested paths do not pass UsageLimits at all; default PAI request_limit=50 counts backend requests and tool_calls_limit=None.

OGX max_tool_calls limits built-in/MCP operations in one response, not tool discovery or each outer run. When reached it supplies a skipped-call message and lets inference continue; a final text answer avoids an outer output retry, explaining the successful cap=2 experiment.

mcp_servers.timeout=1 is reserved and dropped when LSCore constructs InputToolMCP. OGX supplies neither MCP session nor call timeout. Pinned SDK streamable transport defaults are 30-second connect/write/pool and 300-second read inactivity; no separate MCP RPC total deadline is configured. These defaults are source-derived and constructor-confirmed, not long-duration runtime results. An active stream can exceed an inactivity timeout.

ogx.timeout defaults to 180 seconds for remote OGX service HTTP operations. Library mode does not apply it: the PAI in-process transport uses timeout=None and directly awaits OGX handlers. Neither mode establishes a whole-agent wall-clock deadline.

No aggregate wall-clock timeout is applied around query/stream/A2A agent runs in the inspected paths. HTTP read inactivity limits and the A2A 300-second chunk-idle guard should not be presented as an overall run deadline. Long-running boundary behavior remains unverified.

Streaming-query interruption cancels the owned local asyncio task and persists partial text; A2A task cancellation is explicitly unsupported. This source trace does not demonstrate that remote tool work is stopped or its side effects rolled back. The inspected SDK pending-request cleanup contains no outgoing cancelled notification.

integration_implications: Use counters shared across the entire agent request and pass remaining model/tool allowances into every backend continuation; account for actual downstream calls rather than only backend requests.
Stop/reclassify limit exhaustion explicitly instead of treating it as malformed output and retrying with fresh allowances.
Expose and enforce per-tool deadlines and an aggregate request deadline through supported configuration/extensions, then verify cancellation/cleanup without assuming remote side effects were undone.
Record this as a documented-extension gap for the pinned revision; no LSCore patch was made.

lscore_config_limits.fact: Configuration exposes per-request inference iterations and per-response tool-call defaults; the experiment sets 4 and 6.

lscore_limits_forwarded.fact: prepare_responses_params forwards configured max_infer_iters/max_tool_calls into ResponsesApiParams.

lscore_ogx_extra_body.fact: Both limits are passed in model_settings.extra_body to OGX, rather than being converted into shared aggregate model/tool counters.

lscore_build_agent_defaults.fact: Agent is constructed without an explicit retries setting or application loop budget.

lscore_query_run.fact: The non-streaming endpoint invokes agent.run with conversation_id/deps only: no usage_limits or deadline argument.

lscore_stream_run.fact: Streaming invokes agent.run_stream_events without usage_limits or a deadline argument.

lscore_a2a_run.fact: A2A invokes agent.run_stream_events without usage_limits or deadline argument.

lscore_usage_helper.fact: A helper can create PAI UsageLimits but source search found no caller; the inspected query/stream/A2A paths do not invoke it.

pai_default_usage.fact: Without explicit usage_limits PAI constructs its default UsageLimits.

pai_usage_fields.fact: Default request_limit is 50 and tool_calls_limit is None. PAI tracks calls to its model abstraction, here the OGX Responses backend, rather than each hidden downstream inference round.

pai_default_retries.fact: Retry normalization supplies default=1 to missing output/tool retry budgets; LSCore does not override it.

ogx_new_orchestrator.fact: Each OGX create-response request constructs a per-request MCP session manager and new StreamingResponseOrchestrator using the same forwarded limits.

ogx_iteration_limit.fact: After executing tool calls, n_iter increments; reaching max_infer_iters ends this OGX response as incomplete/max_iterations_exceeded.

ogx_tool_limit.fact: If accumulated_builtin_tool_calls reaches max_tool_calls, OGX skips the operation and adds a model-visible tool message. It continues inference so the model can summarize.

ogx_tool_counter_increment.fact: The backend increments its own built-in/MCP operation count after each attempted server-side tool execution.

pai_no_text_retry.fact: With no text/function output, PAI adds Please return text as validation feedback, consumes an output retry, and requests the backend again.

pai_output_retry_stop.fact: Exceeding the output retry budget raises UnexpectedModelBehavior; one output retry means up to two backend responses in this observed no-text case.

lscore_error_mapping.fact: UnexpectedModelBehavior maps to the generic internal-server-error response.

mcp_timeout_reserved.fact: mcp_servers.timeout explicitly says it is reserved for future OGX timeout support.

mcp_timeout_dropped.fact: LSCore constructs InputToolMCP with URL/label/approval/headers/auth; the configured timeout is not forwarded.

ogx_mcp_session_defaults.fact: OGX opens streamablehttp_client(endpoint,headers=headers) and ClientSession without any timeout parameters.

sdk_streamable_timeouts.fact: The deprecated streamablehttp_client used by OGX defaults to timeout=30 and sse_read_timeout=300, creating httpx.Timeout(30,read=300). These are HTTP operation/inactivity settings, not a whole-run deadline.

sdk_call_timeout.fact: ClientSession.call_tool defaults its per-call read_timeout_seconds to None and passes it to send_request.

sdk_rpc_deadline.fact: If neither request nor session timeout is supplied, send_request uses anyio.fail_after(None): no separate RPC total timeout.

sdk_rpc_cleanup.fact: send_request cleanup removes response/progress streams; this path contains no outgoing cancellation notification or side-effect rollback.

ogx_timeout_config.fact: ogx.timeout defaults to 180 seconds and is described as timeout for requests to the OGX service.

ogx_remote_timeout.fact: Only service-mode loader passes config.timeout into AsyncOgxClient.

ogx_library_loader.fact: Library loader creates AsyncOGXAsLibraryClient without passing config.timeout.

ogx_provider_library_timeout.fact: Library-mode PAI transport explicitly creates HTTPX client timeout=None and invokes in-process OGX routes.

ogx_library_dispatch.fact: The library transport directly awaits the selected handler; no total deadline is applied here.

ogx_remote_provider.fact: Service-mode provider reuses the OGX SDK HTTP client, preserving its transport timeout.

ogx_sdk_http_timeout.fact: The OGX SDK applies configured timeout to HTTPX; this is an HTTP operation timeout, not an aggregate agent-run budget.

stream_interrupt.fact: LSCore exposes a separate streaming-query interrupt endpoint.

stream_interrupt_cancel.fact: The interrupt registry checks ownership, cancels the local asyncio task, and schedules partial-result persistence.

stream_interrupted_persistence.fact: The streaming generator catches CancelledError, persists partial text, and emits an interrupted event.

a2a_stream_idle.fact: The A2A stream adapter waits at most 300 seconds for the next queue chunk and cancels the app task on teardown. This is a chunk-idle guard, not a whole-run deadline or implemented A2A task cancellation.
